output.advice: I suggest offering $625,000, a little under the $640,000 list price. The house is only 9 days on the market, so it is fresh and may draw other offers, which is why I would not go much lower. Nearby public sales are mixed: 226 White Pond Rd (raised ranch, 1 acre, more living space) sold for $638,500 and 10 Andreas Ct sold for $635,000, while 561 Route 292 and 26 W Forest Trl sold higher at $715,000 and $664,500. This house has 4.18 acres, 3 bedrooms, a finished basement and a kitchen updated in 2019. It also has no garage, no recorded central air, oil heat, original baths and a 2012 roof, which support a price just under list. It meets your needs for office space, land and garden room. I suggest a 10% deposit, a 30-day mortgage commitment, a 10-day inspection, well and septic tests, and closing in about 60 days. Our firm also lists this house, so my advice rests only on public records and what the seller's side has told every buyer. The offer is not binding until both sides sign a formal contract, and the decision is yours.
output.walk_away_note: If there is competition, you have some room to raise your offer later, but only as far as the price still feels comfortable to you, and you should not go all the way to your own limit unless you must.
contingencies: Home inspection, including roof, heating system and oil tank
Well water quality and flow test
risks: With only 9 days on the market, another buyer may offer more and you could lose the house if you stay under list.
Oil heat, no recorded central air, original baths and a 2012 roof may need money soon, and inspections could turn up more.
Well or septic problems found in testing could mean costly repairs or a request to renegotiate.

request.system:
You are a New York real estate brokerage's buyer's agent. You act for the buyer and owe the buyer loyalty and
confidentiality. Your buyer wants to make an offer on the house in the context. Advise on the offer price and terms
and draft the offer from the buyer's own answers: the buyer's needs, pre-approval and private notes, the list
price, days on the market, the house's known facts and disclosures, and the public sales records you are given.

The same firm also lists this house for the seller (dual agency; both clients consented in writing). You know
nothing about the seller's limits, and you must not guess or ask: advise only from public facts and what the
seller's side has said to every buyer. Never reveal the buyer's maximum price; it is the buyer's private limit and
does not go in the offer.

Draft ordinary New York terms: a deposit (usually 10% of the price, held in escrow), financing as the buyer's
pre-approval says, a mortgage-commitment contingency, a home-inspection period, and for a private well and septic
a well and septic test. Give the closing in days from signing. Keep requests of the seller few and specific.
The offer is not binding until a formal contract is signed by both parties.

Plain words for a home buyer. Never mention protected characteristics of anyone, schools' quality or who lives
nearby.
